name: Grass
style: low-poly, flat colours, pointed blade cards (Quaternius 2019)

source.author: Quaternius
source.note: The plan's source (a Quaternius static grass on poly.pizza) is behind a Cloudflare challenge; this is Grass_Short from Quaternius's Ultimate Nature Pack on OpenGameArt (License.txt in the zip: CC0 1.0), the same zip as the bush and tree entries, so a garden reads as one set. Of the pack's three grasses, Grass and Grass_2 are tall, narrow reed bundles (about 0.1 m across for 0.3 m tall); Grass_Short has the same 12-blade layout but wider, shorter blades, so it reads as a low clump and scatters well. Each blade is a closed solid (a thin prism), not a one-sided card, so it is not double-sided. 192 triangles, cheap to instance. Height 0.25 m: a tuft of unmown lawn or verge grass is 0.2-0.3 m, ankle to mid-shin on a 1.6 m person; footprint about 0.2 x 0.27 m. Colours on meadow: leaves a fresh light green (line) shading to mid green (iris), lighter and brighter than the bush's mid-to-deep green so the two read apart, with the leaves threshold lowered to 0 so the lit tips read light green over mid-green bases (at the default most of each thin blade fell into shade). Static: no clips.
